title: Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints
title_zh: 适应任意测试时预算约束的多轮智能体奖励设计

paragraphs.en: 研究通过多种超支惩罚奖励设计，训练智能体在多轮交互中自主学习分配预算，显著提升预算内成功率与自然合规性。 Large language model agents are often given an inference budget and asked to maximise success within it. A multi-turn agent has to allocate this budget across many environment interactions. An external harness can enforce the budget, but it remains unclear whether the agent itself can learn when and how much to spend. We ask whether agents can learn this allocation across dynamically specified budgets and which rewards best teach this behaviour. We adapt existing length penalties to budget constraints spanning multiple resource types, introduce new reward formulations, and compare eleven objectives in a shared training pipeline. We train Qwen3.5 models at 4B and 9B on AppWorld with budgets over tokens, API calls, and environment steps, and on the BabyAI gridworld with turn budgets. We train a separate policy for each environment and resource type, with each policy trained across budget values. Training with rewards that penalise overspending substantially improves within-budget success and natural compliance over untrained models and over training on task success alone, with agents learning to adapt their resource use to stated budgets and task difficulty. These gains extend to unseen budgets and, zero-shot, to a shifted task distribution and a new benchmark. Reward objectives trade off success within budget and natural compliance. A sigmoid penalty for overspending most often achieves the highest within-budget success at an individual budget, while a fixed negative reward for overspending generally yields the strongest natural compliance. Combining penalties for overspend frequency and magnitude gives the smallest average gap to the best method at each budget. Overall, we show that a single agent can learn to allocate resources across turns and adapt its behaviour to user-specified budgets using budget feedback without external budget-allocation controllers.
paragraphs.zh: 研究通过多种超支惩罚奖励设计，训练智能体在多轮交互中自主学习分配预算，显著提升预算内成功率与自然合规性。大语言模型智能体通常会被给予一个推理预算，并要求在该预算内最大化成功率。 多轮智能体必须将这一预算分配到多次环境交互之中。 外部框架可以强制执行预算，但智能体自身能否学会何时花费以及花费多少，仍不清楚。 我们探究智能体能否学会在动态指定的预算之间进行这种分配，以及哪些奖励最能教会这种行为。 我们将现有的长度惩罚改造为涵盖多种资源类型的预算约束，引入新的奖励公式，并在共享的训练流程中比较十一种目标函数。 我们在 AppWorld 上以 token、API 调用和环境步数预算训练 4B 和 9B 的 Qwen3.5 模型，并在 BabyAI 网格世界（gridworld）上以轮次预算进行训练。 我们为每个环境和资源类型分别训练一个策略，且每个策略都在多个预算取值上进行训练。 与未训练的模型以及仅以任务成功为训练目标的模型相比，使用惩罚超支的奖励进行训练显著提升了预算内成功率和自然合规性，智能体学会根据声明的预算和任务难度调整其资源使用。 这些收益可以扩展到未见过的预算，并且在零样本情况下扩展到发生偏移的任务分布和一个新的基准。 不同的奖励目标在预算内成功率与自然合规性之间存在权衡。 对于超支使用 Sigmoid 惩罚在单个预算下最常取得最高的预算内成功率，而对超支使用固定的负奖励通常带来最强的自然合规性。 将超支频率与超支幅度的惩罚相结合，在各预算下与最优方法的平均差距最小。 总体而言，我们证明单个智能体能够利用预算反馈学会跨轮次分配资源，并使其行为适应用户指定的预算，而无需外部预算分配控制器。
